title: Practice: volume
intro: Nine questions, including one where you build a cuboid to a target volume.

questions.prompt: A prism has a cross-section of area $60\ \text{m}^2$ and is $15\ \text{m}$ long. Find its volume.
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius $3\ \text{cm}$ and height $10\ \text{cm}$. Use $\pi = 3.14$.
hints: Find the circle's area first: $\pi r^2$.
questions.explanation: $V = \pi r^2 h = 3.14 \times 3^2 \times 10 = 28.26 \times 10 = 282.6\ \text{cm}^3$ — about the size of a small drinks can.

questions.prompt: Set the sliders to build a cuboid with volume exactly $60\ \text{cm}^3$, using length $5$, width $4$ and height $3$.
questions.explanation: $5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60\ \text{cm}^3$. Other combinations also give 60 — try $10 \times 3 \times 2$ afterwards and compare the surface areas. Same volume, very different amount of packaging.

questions.scenario: A cylinder has volume $1570\ \text{cm}^3$ and height $20\ \text{cm}$. Use $\pi = 3.14$.

steps.prompt: First work out $\pi \times h$, that is $3.14 \times 20$.
Now divide the volume by that to find $r^2$.

questions.prompt: A tank measures $50\ \text{cm} \times 40\ \text{cm} \times 30\ \text{cm}$. How many **litres** does it hold?
Match each prism to its volume formula.
hints: The last one is the general rule; the other three are it applied to particular shapes.
questions.explanation: All four are really the same formula. Substitute the right cross-sectional area into $A \times h$ and you get each of the others.

hints: A metre is 100 cm — but volume has three dimensions.
questions.explanation: $1\ \text{cm}^3 = 1$ ml, $1$ litre $= 1000\ \text{cm}^3$, and $1\ \text{m}^3 = 100^3 = 1\,000\,000\ \text{cm}^3$. The last one surprises people because all three dimensions scale by 100.

questions.prompt: A triangular prism has a cross-section with base $8\ \text{cm}$ and height $5\ \text{cm}$, and it is $12\ \text{cm}$ long. What is its volume?
hints: Find the area of the triangle first: $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5$.
Then multiply by the 12 cm length.
questions.explanation: Cross-section $= \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 = 20\ \text{cm}^2$, so $V = 20 \times 12 = 240\ \text{cm}^3$. Option **b** forgets to halve the triangle.

questions.prompt: Complete the table for cylinders. Use $\pi = 3.14$ and round volumes to 1 decimal place.
hints: Volume is that area times the height.
questions.explanation: Row by row: $3.14 \times 4 = 12.56$, $\times 5 = 62.8$. $3.14 \times 25 = 78.5$, $\times 4 = 314$. $3.14 \times 100 = 314$, $\times 2 = 628$. Notice rows 2 and 3 — doubling the radius while halving the height *doubles* the volume, because the radius is squared.
